topics: long context handling and KV/prefix caching
transcript:
Header: 2026-07-16 15:30 UTC | Duration: 63 minutes | Recording: on
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Marisol Gomez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (NexaPay), Alyssa Chen (NexaPay SRE), Marco Ruiz (NexaPay ML), Dana Price (NexaPay Procurement)

00:00:12 Priya Shah: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: quick qual, then ethan will run through the console + api demos, then a synthetic high tps test and backpressure example, and finish with q&a and next steps. sound good?
00:00:25 Samir Patel: yep sounds good, and we have 60 minutes so appreciate keeping it tight. small note, we really want to see p95 under bursts and how streaming handles long conversations, like our 100k token session, i mean 100k... not high, sorry 100k-ish context sim.
00:00:45 Ethan Li: 100k, ok noted. there might be some transcription there—kv cache and prefix caching will be key.
00:01:05 Marisol Gomez: also we'll show the Optimize suggestions for quantization and batching for that workload.

00:02:10 Samir Patel: small background, we run payment dispute flows that keep a full session history for customers, sometimes append multi-turn logs up to very long contexts. typical TPS is 400-800 but during promotions we see spikes to ~2k for 10-20 mins. p95 target is 350ms, p99 is more relaxed.
00:02:42 Alyssa Chen: add to that, our infra teams require predictable CPU/GPU scheduling; we want to avoid sudden OOMs and stream timeouts that bubble into the app layer.
00:03:01 Ethan Li: great. i'm going to share the browser, you'll see the console. first, model selection: we have small, medium, and high-capacity variants. for long context we recommend a medium+ with kv cache enabled, or a chunked approach with streaming and prefix caches.
00:03:30 Ethan Li: (screen) ok, Console -> Routes -> Route config. here you can set batching window, max tokens per request, and enable prefix caching. we'll demo the synthetic runner to show the effect.
00:04:05 Marco Ruiz: quick q: does prefix cache persist across sessions or per-connection?
00:04:13 Ethan Li: per route and cache ttl, so you can persist across requests as long as your keys match your session identifier. ttl default is 24h but configurable.
00:04:29 Marco Ruiz: ok good.

00:05:40 Ethan Li: now the API demo. i'll kick off a long-context session with a 75k token prompt (synthetic text). streaming enabled, chunk size 2k tokens. watch the streaming events and the server side telemetry.
00:06:12 (synthetic run started)
00:06:25 Speaker 2: um the stream is starting... you can see server got a partial chunk, then assembled to the model...
00:07:08 Ethan Li: so at ~30 seconds you should see the first partial tokens. notice the RTT from customer side is about 120ms but server processing jumps when kv cache miss occurs.
00:07:41 Alyssa Chen: after a cache miss, do you rehydrate from storage or recompute?
00:07:47 Ethan Li: rehydrate from the KV backing store if we have it (fast path) else it will recompute transiently which increases latency. that's why pre-warming and pinned prefills help.

00:09:00 Ethan Li: now switching to the high-TPS stress test. hitting route with 2k rps sustained for 5 minutes. watch the meter and the backpressure events.
00:09:30 (load generator: run id 2026-07-16-9a)
00:10:02 Marisol Gomez: you'll see the batching efficiency improve token cost but it will increase per-request latency slightly — tradeoff.
00:10:27 Samir Patel: during pubic spikes we can't accept >500ms tail in the auth flow, so what are the guardrails?
00:10:38 Ethan Li: several: 1) per-route concurrency limits, 2) backpressure (reject or queue) policies, 3) automatic fallback to a smaller model for non-critical tokens, and 4) circuit-breaker into a cached response for idempotent calls.
00:11:02 Marco Ruiz: can you show fallback in action?
00:11:08 Ethan Li: yes, triggering fallback now. i will set route policy to fallback-to-small when queue depth > 50.
00:11:36 (policy applied)
00:11:45 (load generator)
00:12:10 Priya Shah: note that fallback preserves schema but output may be lower quality; good for classification or intent endpoints, not long-form summaries.
00:13:00 Alyssa Chen: we saw a stream timeout in a previous POC — can you show how timeouts surface and how retries are handled?
00:13:17 Ethan Li: ok simulating network drop and also server-side timeouts. first, client-side: streaming read times out, browser aborts, client retries with exponential backoff. server will attempt to resume if KV cache present, otherwise full recompute.
00:13:48 (simulated network flakiness)
00:14:10 Speaker 3: uh we got a 504 there, stream aborted mid-token, recovery attempted.
00:14:35 Marisol Gomez: that's where our 'resume token' support helps — we can resume from last acked kv position to reduce recompute.

00:16:20 Ethan Li: switching to Optimize tab: the system auto-suggests batching windows based on request size distribution. for NexaPay we recommended batch window 30ms and batch size 4 for mid-traffic, and a separate profile for burst traffic favoring smaller batches and more concurrency.
00:16:48 Samir Patel: will optimize change at runtime or need manual ack?
00:16:53 Marisol Gomez: Optimize suggests, auto-apply is opt-in. we can enable adaptive profiles per route with safe rollback.

00:18:05 (second load run: 2k rps spike for 10 minutes)
00:18:45 Ethan Li: observe the backpressure queue length rising at minute 2, we hit concurrency cap on the pool. at minute 3 we start to fallback to smaller model for low-priority routes.
00:19:10 Alyssa Chen: can you point to the logs that show where the timeout bubbled?
00:19:16 Ethan Li: sure — in tracing view: request span shows wait_for_execution then prefill_io then compute. look for span attribute 'prefill_miss=true' and 'fallback_triggered=true'.
00:19:44 Marco Ruiz: there's some noise in the transcript but seeing the trace. question: if fallback occurs mid-stream, do we close with a coherent output or partial?
00:19:55 Ethan Li: we close the stream gracefully with a final partial and a note in the metadata that fallback happened; client can choose to retry with a stronger model synchronously.

00:21:05 Samir Patel: about cost: if you fallback to a smaller model during spikes, how do we account billing and attribution?
00:21:14 Priya Shah: billing is by token + model variant. fallback is reflected in route-level metrics and cost breakout; you can set policy to prefer cost or quality.

00:23:00 (short pause as SE pulls additional logs)
00:23:30 Ethan Li: ok i'm going to purposely provoke a large OOM style condition by sending a very long single request without prefix caching. you will see the server detect memory pressure and trigger a reject with a 429 or 503 depending on policy.
00:24:12 (synthetic bad request run)
00:24:45 Speaker 4: saw 503 and a note 'memory-pressure-triggered'.
00:25:02 Marisol Gomez: that's expected — you want either chunking at client side or an ingress transformer to split the session into manageable blocks.
00:25:28 Marco Ruiz: will the client library do automatic chunking?
00:25:33 Ethan Li: yes we have an SDK option for 'auto-chunk' which can also keep streaming semantics by sending incremental state and using KV rehydrate on the server.

00:27:10 Alyssa Chen: network topology question: for private deployment in our VPC can we keep KV store local to reduce latency?
00:27:20 Ethan Li: yes, Private supports customer-managed KV/HSM and KMS, and we can run the cache and model serving within a VPC to cut cross-region hops.
00:27:34 Samir Patel: what about auditing? we need full request audit trail exposed to our SIEM.
00:27:41 Priya Shah: we provide audit logs, token-level tracing, and can forward logs to S3/Syslog or your SIEM with retention controls.

00:30:05 (mid-call recap)
00:30:20 Priya Shah: recap: 1) enable prefix caching and pre-warm sessions for long context, 2) use auto-chunking and SDK resume token to reduce recompute and timeouts, 3) set fallback policies for burst spikes, 4) use Optimize profiles to tune batching windows, and 5) consider Dedicated or Private deployment for strict p95 targets.

00:31:00 Samir Patel: procurement angle — what's minimum committed for Dedicated and is there a pilot?
00:31:12 Priya Shah: Dedicated has monthly reserved pools; we offer a pilot with limited commit for evaluation. i'll share exact thresholds in the quote.
00:32:05 Dana Price: legal question — will we get an addendum about data residency and encryption?
00:32:12 Priya Shah: yes, we'll attach the Private deployment addendum and KMS/HSM spec.

00:33:40 (deep-dive: tracing and charts)
00:33:50 Ethan Li: here's the trace where a 2k rps spike caused prefills to fall, notice prefill queue jumping, and kernel selection overhead increased. we mitigated by increasing pool size and enabling per-route pre-warm during predicted windows.
00:34:38 Marco Ruiz: how long to spin up more capacity?
00:34:44 Ethan Li: depends on Dedicated vs Hosted: Dedicated can have autoscaling tuned to <60s spin-ups for burst capacity; hosted falls back to region and compatible model which is faster but less predictable.

00:36:55 Alyssa Chen: any advice on measuring production regressions from Optimize changes? we want safe guards.
00:37:03 Marisol Gomez: we recommend canary with traffic split and quality evals tied to prompt sets; Optimize reports expected token savings and an estimated quality delta.

00:39:10 (small demo: simulate adaptive batching flip)
00:39:45 Ethan Li: adapt flipped, throughput slightly increased but p95 rose 40ms — Optimize warns about that in the console.

00:41:00 Samir Patel: micro question: streaming chunk size of 2k — does that mean 2k tokens in flight?
00:41:09 Ethan Li: it's the chunk emitted to stream; we still manage internal kv pages and the compute kernel may process differently. in practice you tune chunk size with latency and memory constraints.

00:43:20 (customer shares their traffic sample)
00:43:45 Samir Patel: sample shows many short requests with a small percent of sessions that are very long — sounds like power-law. can we route long sessions to a special route?
00:43:59 Ethan Li: yes, route by header or session id. long-session route can have different model, caching, and concurrency profile.

00:46:10 (Q&A wrap)
00:46:28 Marco Ruiz: last technical ask: for resuming streams after a client reconnect, how deterministic is resume across model versions?
00:46:35 Ethan Li: resume is best-effort; for model version changes we maintain a compatibility shim but recommend pinning model version during a session or triggering a controlled migration.

00:48:05 Priya Shah: final checklist — i'll share the quote, ethan will send the runner logs + runbook, samir will send traffic dump; marisol will propose Optimize profiles. any other items?
00:48:28 Dana Price: procurement needs lead time for legal — we'll aim to review docs by end of week.
00:48:45 Priya Shah: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with attachments and links.

00:50:00 (meeting ends but recording kept for a few mins)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mislabels and stutters; some product names transcribed as 'kv cache' vs 'k v cache' etc.

End of transcript.
